summary: Enoch grounds moral objectivity in stance-independent facts and ordinary deliberation, while confronting rival-package, noncognitivist, and reflective-anomaly challenges to action guidance.

pro.text: you've come to the conclusion that you ought to do it
pro.context: Enoch uses the first-person perspective to argue that reaching an ought-conclusion normally completes deliberation, even though weakness of will may still prevent action.

con.text: knowledge of the ethical facts as David was just suggesting
con.context: Clarke-Doane identifies the realist promise under examination before arguing that rival normative packages can preserve a further deliberative question.

pro-ordinary-stance-independence.words: Ordinary judgments that humiliation is wrong present that wrongness as independent of anyone's preferences, social conventions, beliefs, or practices.
pro-ordinary-stance-independence.critique: Strongest feature: The everyday humiliation example sharply separates moral wrongness from personal liking, communal convention, counterfactual belief, and prevailing practice, while the explicit qualification prevents this discourse premise from pretending already to demonstrate a complete realist metaphysics. Principal limitation: Illustrative linguistic evidence cannot establish how consistently ordinary speakers understand moral claims, and independence from familiar stances does not alone identify robust normative facts as the uniquely adequate explanation. Live burden: The argument must connect this carefully bounded characterization of ordinary objectivity to an affirmative ontology while answering the possibility that another theory could preserve the same independence. Locked score: The very strong band reflects excellent conceptual precision, direct contact with a central bridge, and disciplined calibration, tempered by limited empirical breadth and an intentionally incomplete realist inference.

pro-deliberative-indispensability.words: Normative truths are indispensable to the respectable project of practical deliberation, analogously to explanatory posits, and thereby acquire ontological respectability.
pro-deliberative-indispensability.critique: Strongest feature: The analogy between explanatory inquiry and practical deliberation provides an affirmative route to normative ontology, presenting deliberation as a respectable project whose indispensable commitments merit ontological recognition rather than resting realism upon linguistic appearances. Principal limitation: The abbreviated electron comparison leaves the relevant indispensability insufficiently characterized and does not demonstrate why indispensability within practical reasoning warrants ontological commitment instead of project-internal usefulness. Live burden: The argument must establish parity between explanatory and deliberative indispensability while demonstrating that normative facts perform indispensable work unavailable to attitude-centered or deflationary alternatives. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects central relevance and a constructive mechanism, moderated because the analogy's sufficiency claim remains stronger than its articulated justification.

con-objectivity-exceeds-mind-independenc.words: Stance-independent moral properties do not alone secure action-settling objectivity, because convention-independent rival normative packages can leave deliberation unresolved.
con-objectivity-exceeds-mind-independenc.critique: Strongest feature: The reply precisely distinguishes ordinary mind independence from the stronger action-settling objectivity required by the motion, preserves realism's genuine achievement, and directly tests whether recognized normative facts complete deliberation when rival convention-independent packages remain intelligible. Principal limitation: Its moral-twin iteration establishes a coherent possibility more readily than an independently evidenced prevalence or unavoidable feature of practical reasoning, so the gap's generality remains less firmly demonstrated than its intelligibility. Live burden: The account must explain why allegiance among rival packages remains substantively deliberative rather than merely redescribing uncertainty, error, or incomplete normative knowledge. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional motion-level relevance, comprehensive responsiveness, stable qualification, and charitable representation, moderated principally by the conceptual rather than independently corroborated evidential basis.

pro-generalized-package-challenge.words: Because the rival-package objection generalizes throughout normativity and generates repeated higher-order questions, its apparent deliberative gap may depend on a false presupposition.
pro-generalized-package-challenge.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly contests the rival-package objection at its governing level, using unrestricted generalization and repeated higher-order iteration to motivate the calibrated suspicion that the supposed residual question may arise from a defective framing rather than genuine deliberative incompleteness. Principal limitation: The speaker expressly cannot identify the alleged false presupposition, so generality and iteration remain diagnostic clues instead of a criterion showing why the opposing question is unintelligible or illegitimate. Live burden: The response must distinguish harmless repetition from substantive regress and explain what licenses deliberative closure without merely redescribing the recurring challenge as a pseudo-problem. Locked score: The strong and competent band recognizes decisive relevance, candid uncertainty, and substantial responsiveness, while withholding stronger evaluation because the central defeating premise is asserted conditionally but never specified.

con-metaphysical-privilege-dilemma.words: Metaphysical privilege cannot select an action-guiding package: nonnormative privilege is practically inert, whereas normative privilege recreates the selection question at another level.
con-metaphysical-privilege-dilemma.critique: Strongest feature: The dilemma supplies the con route's clearest mechanism, dividing metaphysical privilege into nonnormative and normative forms and explaining why the former lacks practical authority while the latter renews the privilege-versus-privilege-star question instead of terminating it. Principal limitation: The constructed horns receive targeted conceptual support, but practical inertness and recursive instability are not independently established, and a realist may contend that fundamental normative privilege legitimately ends explanation. Live burden: The reply must show that asking which higher-order standard governs is a genuine practical question rather than an indefinitely repeatable verbal demand applicable to every position. Locked score: The very strong band reflects decisive motion contact, unusually complete responsiveness, conceptual precision, and fair treatment of the realist endpoint, with evidential compression preventing an even stronger assessment.

pro-normative-metaphysical-privilege.words: Metaphysical privilege may itself be normative, and renewed questions about privilege versus privilege-star repeat the original purported pseudo-problem rather than advancing it.
pro-normative-metaphysical-privilege.critique: Strongest feature: The response squarely chooses the normative horn of the privilege dilemma, clarifies that normativity can fall within metaphysics, and accurately identifies the higher-order privilege-versus-privilege-star question as the decisive point requiring an answer. Principal limitation: Calling the renewed question a pseudo-problem does not provide a stable criterion separating empty iteration from a coherent rival standard, especially when the speaker acknowledges that the maneuver produces no evident progress. Live burden: The reply must explain why privileged normative facts legitimately terminate deliberation and why privilege-star fails to generate an equally intelligible practical demand. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects direct engagement with the central objection, explicit qualifications, and accurate representation, but also comparatively weak warrant and coherence where the crucial regress-blocking explanation is replaced by a contested label.

pro-comparative-alternative-burden.words: A difficulty shared by every plausible metanormative theory does not discriminate against realism unless a comparatively superior alternative handles it better overall.
pro-comparative-alternative-burden.critique: Strongest feature: The reply establishes a disciplined comparative standard, correctly observing that a challenge shared across remotely plausible metanormative positions cannot by itself select against realism, while the immediate retreat from an initially stronger formulation demonstrates unusually careful calibration. Principal limitation: The move does not independently establish that every plausible alternative inherits the same difficulty, and common failure would remove discriminatory force without showing that action-settling objectivity is an illegitimate requirement. Live burden: The argument must evaluate the proposed attitude-centered alternative and demonstrate either equivalent residual difficulties or offsetting costs in its account of ordinary objectivity. Locked score: The very strong band reflects excellent responsiveness, logical structure, representational fairness, and burden relevance, with the remaining limitation confined to evidential support for the universal comparative premise rather than the comparison's validity.

pro-limits-of-theoretical-guidance.words: Metaethical adequacy requires truth and plausibility, not an ability to extract every confused, mistaken, or skeptical agent from any residual practical uncertainty.
pro-limits-of-theoretical-guidance.critique: Strongest feature: The reply offers a principled methodological reframe by denying that metaethical adequacy requires universal therapeutic guidance for every mistaken or skeptical agent and substituting the more defensible constraints of theoretical truth and plausibility. Principal limitation: The skepticism analogy does not establish that the opponent's informed reflective cases are confused, and it risks weakening a challenge about promised action settlement into an excessive demand for persuading absolutely everyone. Live burden: The response must show why residual deliberation among informed agents is theoretically peripheral or explainable without abandoning realism's claimed connection between ought-conclusions and action guidance. Locked score: The strong and competent band rewards a coherent stopping principle, explicit scope, and meaningful subsidiary relevance, while recognizing reduced charity, limited analogical support, and incomplete contact with the central reflective counterexample.

con-decision-centered-noncognitivism.words: An attitude-centered view identifies what one ought to do with deciding or prescribing action, so adopting one option excludes incompatible alternatives without further package allegiance.
con-decision-centered-noncognitivism.critique: Strongest feature: The proposal answers the comparative-alternative demand directly by locating practical closure in deciding, prescribing, or adopting an action-directed attitude, thereby explaining structurally how one selected action excludes incompatible alternatives without relying on another truth-apt property's metaphysical privilege. Principal limitation: Building exclusion into the relevant attitude does not yet demonstrate that the attitude preserves ordinary objectivity, outperforms realist first-person closure, or avoids merely stipulating the desired connection between judgment and action. Live burden: The alternative must distinguish deliberative settlement from causal execution, accommodate akrasia, and specify how warranted criticism remains possible across conflicting prescriptions. Locked score: The very strong band recognizes central comparative relevance, coherent architecture, and broad responsiveness, while the proposal's acknowledged complications and underdeveloped objectivity-preserving resources constrain its evidential warrant.

pro-noncognitivist-objectivity-costs.words: An attitude-centered noncognitivism that preserves commonsense moral objectivity requires additional theoretical commitments whose plausibility and comparative cost must be assessed.
pro-noncognitivist-objectivity-costs.critique: Strongest feature: The objection directly restores the comparative burden omitted by a decision-centered alternative, insisting that structural proximity to action is not sufficient if preserving commonsense moral objectivity requires further semantic, psychological, or practical resources. Principal limitation: The source span neither inventories those additional commitments nor demonstrates that their combined cost exceeds realism's own ontological and deliberative commitments, leaving the claimed comparative disadvantage substantially programmatic. Live burden: The reply must specify what objectivity-preserving machinery noncognitivism needs and compare its explanatory performance against realism under common criteria rather than treating added structure itself as disqualifying. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects central relevance, appropriate conditional framing, and charitable openness about possible resources, tempered by evidential underdevelopment and a somewhat stronger cost implication than the supplied particulars warrant.

pro-first-person-deliberative-closure.words: When a first-person deliberator concludes that an action ought to be done, deliberation normally closes, although weakness of will may still prevent performance.
pro-first-person-deliberative-closure.critique: Strongest feature: The first-person test reaches the motion's action-guidance demand directly, cleanly distinguishing completion of deliberation from successful execution and expressly allowing both akrasia and variation in individual phenomenology. Principal limitation: Ordinary phenomenological closure does not itself establish that stance-independent facts non-causally settle every informed reflective dispute, particularly where an agent understands rival standards and experiences a substantive allegiance question. Live burden: The argument must explain why exceptional rival-framework cases do not reveal a structural gap, or else defend normal deliberative closure as the proportionate kind of objectivity realism promises. Locked score: The very strong band reflects outstanding motion relevance, precise qualifications, strong responsiveness, and a coherent experiential mechanism, while reserving room because its evidential base privileges ordinary first-person cases over the opponent's strongest informed counterexamples.

con-deflationary-attitude-semantics.words: An attitude-centered noncognitivism can adopt deflationism and avoid inheriting the elaborate semantic machinery commonly associated with standard expressivist accounts.
con-deflationary-attitude-semantics.critique: Strongest feature: The reply narrows a potentially overbroad comparative objection by separating the proposed attitude-centered position from standard expressivist semantics and candidly presenting deflationism as an alternative orientation rather than pretending to have supplied a completed semantic theory. Principal limitation: Deflationism remains an underdefined pitch in the excerpt, leaving unexplained how the view handles compositional practice, disagreement, objectivity, practical psychology, and the other commitments implicated by the pro challenge. Live burden: The account must specify enough positive machinery to demonstrate genuine theoretical economy without quietly relocating complexity from semantics into pragmatics or attitudes. Locked score: The strong/competent band reflects clear subsidiary relevance, fair contact with a recognizable cost, appropriately limited asserted force, and stable scope, tempered by comparatively thin explanation and incomplete comparative evaluation.

con-reflective-logic-counterexample.words: An informed agent can know that an inference is classically valid yet recognize its invalidity under a rival logic, leaving rational settlement distinct from causal inference.
con-reflective-logic-counterexample.critique: Strongest feature: The rival-logics case directly challenges first-person deliberative closure with a structured informed counterexample, carefully separating causal production of an inference from its non-causal rational settlement when competing consequence relations classify the same transition differently. Principal limitation: The example defeats an unrestricted necessity claim more clearly than the realist's qualified normality claim, and its transfer from exceptionally reflective logical disputes to ordinary moral deliberation requires additional defense. Live burden: The counterexample must establish that the residual choice is practically substantive and sufficiently analogous to normative-package allegiance, rather than a localized uncertainty about the correct logic. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional direct responsiveness, recoverable distinctions, proportionate possibility-level force, and charitable recognition of ordinary closure, with comparative rarity and cross-domain applicability limiting the warrant.

pro-centrality-weighted-theory-cost.words: Awkwardly accommodating rare reflective cases costs a theory less than failing to explain central features of ordinary normative and deliberative practice.
pro-centrality-weighted-theory-cost.critique: Strongest feature: The reply concedes the reflective anomaly and offers a comparative principle: explanatory awkwardness concerning exceptional cases can be less damaging than inability to capture foundational features of normative deliberation. Principal limitation: Centrality remains asserted rather than specified, while the response insufficiently addresses how a foundational anomaly might disclose a structural defect whose importance substantially exceeds its prevalence. Live burden: The weighting method must distinguish explanatory centrality from familiarity and demonstrate why rival-framework cases remain peripheral to the phenomenon realism purports to explain. Locked score: The very strong band recognizes central relevance, direct responsiveness, explicit concession, and proportionate calibration, while evidential and charitable limitations concern justification of comparative weights rather than the coherence of weighting theoretical costs.

con-informed-deliberator-method.words: The importance of a deliberative anomaly should be tested among agents who understand the problem, rather than inferred from its absence among an unreflective majority.
con-informed-deliberator-method.critique: Strongest feature: The methodological reply identifies a relevant population for testing reflective anomalies, explaining why raw prevalence among people unfamiliar with the problem cannot determine whether informed deliberation contains a persistent structural gap. Principal limitation: Awareness is not yet operationalized as understanding, no selection or measurement procedure is supplied, and specialist responses might reflect training artifacts rather than a central feature of practical reasoning. Live burden: The method must define informed competence, compare responses systematically, and show why those responses illuminate deliberation's explanatory structure without replacing centrality with a different headcount. Locked score: The strong/competent band reflects meaningful contact with anomaly weighting, a plausible and tentatively calibrated methodological insight, and charitable engagement, while sparse evidence and an undeveloped sampling criterion substantially restrict its independent force.

con-foundational-anomaly-significance.words: Rare, apparently baroque foundational anomalies may expose transformative structural defects and therefore cannot receive negligible weight merely because ordinary practice otherwise succeeds.
con-foundational-anomaly-significance.critique: Strongest feature: The reply resists frequency-based discounting through foundational analogies, explaining how an apparently baroque anomaly can disclose a transformative defect even when ordinary practice functions smoothly, while restating the possible deliberative distance between knowing a fact and regulating behavior by it. Principal limitation: Russell-style and scientific-change comparisons establish possible significance, not that this particular normative anomaly is comparably foundational, so the analogy still needs a domain-specific bridge. Live burden: The argument must demonstrate that rival-package deliberation reveals the architecture of normative guidance rather than merely an exceptional complication at its theoretical margins. Locked score: The very strong band reflects direct engagement with centrality weighting, concrete analogical support, careful possibility-level calibration, and strong charity, moderated by the unfinished inference from foundational exemplars to the target phenomenon.

pro-explanatory-not-contradictory-cost.words: The alleged deliberative gap is an explanatory imperfection rather than a contradiction, so its theoretical cost appropriately varies with the centrality of the affected phenomenon.
pro-explanatory-not-contradictory-cost.critique: Strongest feature: The response articulates a principled distinction between logical inconsistency and uneven explanatory naturalness, explaining why localized awkwardness may be weighted by phenomenological centrality while contradiction constitutes a different theoretical liability. Principal limitation: The classification remains contestable because an opponent may regard contradictions as defeasible costs and contend that reflective anomalies reveal foundational explanatory damage rather than roughness. Live burden: The argument must substantiate both its noncontradictory diagnosis and a principled centrality measure that assigns substantial significance whenever an exceptional case genuinely transforms the understanding. Locked score: The very strong band reflects clear conceptual structure, direct responsiveness, burden relevance, and comparative support, tempered by underdeveloped weighting criteria and the possibility that the anomaly's foundational significance remains understated.

con-contradictions-as-defeasible-costs.words: Paraconsistent logic shows that contradiction can be a defeasible theoretical price rather than automatic defeat, placing it on a continuum with explanatory anomalies.
con-contradictions-as-defeasible-costs.critique: Strongest feature: The reply contests the categorical contrast through paraconsistent logic, showing contradiction as survivable and defeasible, thereby supporting comparative evaluation of logical and explanatory costs rather than automatic theoretical defeat. Principal limitation: Survivability cannot establish that contradictions and ordinary explanatory awkwardness inhabit a homogeneous continuum, since contradictions may preserve distinctive inferential consequences even where explosion is blocked. Live burden: The position must articulate principled dimensions for comparing heterogeneous costs and demonstrate their application to the deliberative anomaly, rather than resting on abstract logical possibility. Locked score: The very strong band reflects recognizable conceptual support, explicit qualification, close engagement with the opposing distinction, and proportionate force, while compressed applicability and the unresolved severity comparison constrain its broader contribution.

strengths: Established a carefully qualified account of ordinary stance independence without pretending that discourse evidence alone completed the realist ontology.
Kept the exchange comparative by demanding that rival views demonstrate superior overall handling rather than merely identifying a difficulty potentially shared across theories.
Directly connected ought-judgment with first-person deliberative closure while clearly distinguishing completed deliberation from weakness of will or failed execution.
Conceded exceptional reflective anomalies and developed a coherent centrality-sensitive method for comparing their explanatory cost with failures concerning ordinary practice.
Repeatedly calibrated claims through explicit qualifications, including retreats from overstrong formulations and acknowledgment of phenomenological variation.

blunders.text: The rival-package replies repeatedly characterized iteration as a pseudo-problem without supplying the stable criterion needed to distinguish illegitimate repetition from a genuine higher-order practical question.
The indispensability argument compressed the bridge from usefulness in deliberation to ontological respectability, leaving the claimed parity with explanatory posits insufficiently defended.
The objection to noncognitivism invoked unspecified additional commitments, preventing a concrete comparison between those costs and realism's own theoretical commitments.

strengths: Distinguished mind-independent truth from action-settling objectivity and consistently connected that distinction to the motion's demanding deliberative requirement.
Developed a two-horn privilege dilemma that directly answered both the realist ontology and the attempt to dismiss iteration as a pseudo-problem.
Supplied an identifiable attitude-centered alternative, thereby meeting the comparative burden rather than relying exclusively on internal criticism of realism.
Used an informed rival-logics case to separate causal compliance from rational settlement and to challenge universalized first-person closure.
Defended the possible theoretical importance of rare foundational anomalies without overstating them as guaranteed refutations of the realist framework.

blunders.text: The deflationary alternative remained substantially programmatic and did not explain how objectivity, disagreement, compositional practice, and action guidance would be jointly preserved.
The informed-deliberator proposal lacked a developed competence criterion, sampling method, or safeguard against treating specialist artifacts as evidence about deliberation generally.
Several foundational and logical analogies established intelligible possibilities more securely than they established direct applicability to ordinary moral deliberation.

thesis.text: This AI-generated steelman, not transcript content or wording attributable to David Enoch, argues that stance-independent normative facts vindicate action-guiding objectivity when correctly grasped ought-judgments provide reasons whose authority does not require a further independent act of allegiance.

novelty.explanation: It integrates the pro route while explicitly repairing the missing bridge between realist facts, justified normative judgment, and deliberative closure.

premises.text: Ordinary moral judgment presents at least some reasons as answerable to features of conduct rather than to an agent's preferences, communal conventions, or contingent acceptance, creating a substantial explanatory demand for any adequate metanormative theory.

novelty.explanation: It develops the ordinary-stance claim into a comparative explanatory constraint without treating that constraint as a complete proof of realism.

premises.text: Deliberation necessarily treats some considerations as reasons bearing on what to do, and a theory that eliminates their truth-directed authority must explain how practical inquiry remains more than the organization of antecedently favored attitudes.

novelty.explanation: It strengthens the indispensability line by specifying the deliberative function whose theoretical replacement requires explanation.

premises.text: A justified first-person conclusion that one ought to perform an action normally ends the question of what reasons support, even though motivation may fail and unusual agents may reopen inquiry by challenging the conclusion's justification.

novelty.explanation: It preserves normal closure while accommodating informed reopening as a challenge to justification rather than an automatic second allegiance decision.

premises.text: Higher-order demands for choosing between every standard require a reason to believe that a genuine undefeated alternative remains; the mere formal possibility of constructing privilege-star does not establish an additional practical question.

novelty.explanation: It replaces the unsupported pseudo-problem label with an evidential condition for when iteration generates a live deliberative burden.

premises.text: Comparative assessment should weigh breadth, centrality, and severity separately, giving foundational anomalies serious attention without automatically allowing a rare explanatory imperfection to outweigh successful treatment of pervasive deliberative practice.

novelty.explanation: It operationalizes the centrality principle and answers the objection that rarity alone cannot determine theoretical importance.

conclusion.text: Robust realism therefore remains a proportionate account of normative objectivity if it explains stance-independent reasons, their indispensable deliberative role, and normal first-person closure better overall than alternatives while treating reflective anomalies as genuine but defeasible costs.

novelty.explanation: It draws a comparative and defeasible conclusion that is no stronger than the integrated premises support.

newArguments.title: The warranted-reopening distinction
newArguments.text: A residual question matters only when it is supported by a reason to doubt the operative ought-conclusion, not whenever an agent can grammatically ask what to do next. This distinguishes rational reopening from bare iterative questioning. Rival logical or normative frameworks can therefore matter when they expose an unresolved justificatory conflict, while invented privilege-star variants do not automatically create equal alternatives. Realism can acknowledge the former without accepting an endless allegiance requirement for every formally describable standard.

novelty.explanation: This new line supplies an independent criterion separating genuine reflective reopening from merely repeatable questioning.

newArguments.title: Multi-dimensional theoretical cost
newArguments.text: Theoretical costs should be compared along distinct dimensions: how frequently a phenomenon occurs, how central it is to the practice being explained, and how severely the theory misrepresents it. A rare case may be foundational and severe, so frequency cannot settle its weight; conversely, foundational interest does not guarantee that the alleged defect is destructive. This framework lets realism assign real weight to reflective anomalies while still defending its treatment of pervasive first-person deliberation against alternatives with broader objectivity costs.

novelty.explanation: This independently introduces a three-dimensional cost framework that refines the debate's simpler contrast between ordinary centrality and rare anomalies.

newArguments.title: Authority without motivational guarantee
newArguments.text: Action-guiding authority need not mean causal compulsion, guaranteed motivation, or immunity from renewed inquiry. A normative fact guides action when an agent who justifiably grasps it thereby has an answer to the question supported by reasons, even if weakness, distraction, or later evidence changes behavior. This interpretation preserves the distinction between settling what ought to be done and ensuring that it is done, while giving realism a clear standard against which an attitude-centered alternative must demonstrate superior explanatory coverage.

novelty.explanation: It repairs ambiguity about action settlement by separating rational authority, motivation, execution, and later justified reconsideration.

thesis.text: AI steelman: Stance-independent moral facts may secure truth beyond preference while still failing, by themselves, to determine action, because practical settlement requires a justified commitment procedure that selects among intelligible rival normative packages.

novelty.explanation: This steelman repairs the gap argument by adding a positive commitment procedure instead of relying only on recursive challenges to realist privilege.

premises.text: If two stance-independent packages issue incompatible recommendations and an agent understands both, merely identifying which package is metaphysically privileged does not settle action unless that privilege itself supplies a practical reason for allegiance.

novelty.explanation: This develops the distinction between metaphysical ranking and practically action-guiding authority.

premises.text: A nonnormative fact about privilege cannot generate practical authority without a bridge principle, while a normative bridge principle remains assessable under the same question of which normative standard an agent should follow.

novelty.explanation: This makes each horn explicit and identifies the bridge principle required for practical relevance.

premises.text: A decision-centered account can close deliberation without denying truth-apt moral discourse if it distinguishes the representational content considered during reasoning from the action-committing attitude that completes reasoning.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the alternative by separating deliberative representation from the commitment that excludes incompatible actions.

premises.text: Reflective counterexamples matter when they isolate a structural feature of guidance, but their significance should depend on diagnostic relevance and informed reproducibility rather than either population frequency or philosophical vividness alone.

novelty.explanation: This supplies stricter criteria for using rare informed cases and repairs the undeveloped sampling method.

premises.text: Theoretical costs are heterogeneous and defeasible, so comparisons should track inferential disruption, explanatory reach, practical consequences, and repair costs instead of treating contradiction or rarity as categorically decisive.

novelty.explanation: This adds principled dimensions for comparing logical and explanatory anomalies.

conclusion.text: Therefore, realism alone does not yet vindicate action-settling objectivity unless it explains how recognized normative facts rationally authorize allegiance, while a suitably developed decision-centered account remains a credible comparative alternative rather than a completed theory.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion proportionately combines the negative burden on realism with a qualified, nonfinal claim for the alternative.

newArguments.title: Commitment-procedure asymmetry
newArguments.text: A theory can represent reasons accurately yet remain incomplete as a theory of practical settlement if it supplies no account of rational commitment. The relevant comparison is therefore not facts versus attitudes in isolation, but rival procedures for moving from represented considerations to an exclusionary commitment. Realism may contribute indispensable content while an attitude-centered procedure contributes closure. Unless realism explains that transition without presupposing the disputed package, its ontology does not uniquely perform the action-settling work claimed for it.

novelty.explanation: This newly distinguishes representational accuracy from procedural completion and evaluates theories by their allocation of those functions.

newArguments.title: Diagnostic invariance test
newArguments.text: A reflective anomaly deserves substantial weight when it persists under changes that remove merely verbal, sociological, and informational explanations. Test whether informed agents still face the residual question after terminology is standardized, factual ignorance is corrected, consequences are made explicit, and rival standards are represented symmetrically. Persistence across those interventions would support a structural deliberative gap; disappearance would favor the realist diagnosis of confusion or incomplete understanding. This test converts the informed-deliberator suggestion into a comparative method rather than an appeal to specialist reactions.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the sampling proposal with controlled diagnostic conditions and an outcome that can also count against the con position.
